def: A condition on fields stored beside each chunk (tenant, date, language, access list) that a retrieved result must satisfy.
The fraction of a collection that passes a filter, which decides whether pre-filtering, filtered traversal or post-filtering is cheapest.
Running the approximate search first and then discarding results that fail the filter, which can leave fewer than k results.
Applying the filter first and then searching only the passing documents, usually with an exact scan when few documents pass.
Walking an index graph while testing the filter at each node, counting only passing nodes as results but using failing ones as stepping stones.
A search that keeps widening its candidate list until enough rows pass the filter or a work limit is reached.
Ensuring that one customer's documents can never appear in another customer's retrieval, by separate indexes or by mandatory tenant predicates.
Removing from search results every document the caller is not allowed to read, before the results or any text derived from them are shown.
The set of users and groups permitted to read a document, stored with each chunk so retrieval can filter on it.
A hash of a caller's identity set or policy version, included in cache keys so personalised answers are never shared across different permissions.
A planted document with a unique meaningless phrase in a restricted scope, used to detect any leak of that scope.
